reels.hook: Rads cold at the bottom? That's sludge
reels.body: Bleeding won't fix it. Sludge settles at the bottom of the panel.
reels.instagram:
Cold at the TOP is trapped air — bleeding fixes that.

Cold at the BOTTOM is sludge, and no amount of bleeding will shift it. That needs a proper flush.

If half your rad is warm and the bottom stays stone cold, that's the one to get looked at before winter.

reels.hook: Boiler pressure dropped? Fix it yourself
reels.body: Filling loop, both valves, watch the gauge hit 1.2-1.5 bar.

Find the silver braided filling loop under the boiler. Open both valves slowly. Watch the gauge climb to 1.2-1.5 bar. Close both valves.

If it keeps dropping week after week, that's a leak — that one you do need me for.

reels.hook: This came out of a magnetic filter
reels.body: Two years of sludge, caught before it reached the boiler.
reels.instagram:

Every bit of it would otherwise be going through the pump and heat exchanger. It's the cheapest part on the whole system and it saves the most expensive one.

If you haven't got one fitted, ask about it at your next service.

reels.hook: Boiler dead in a cold snap? Check this
reels.body: A frozen condensate pipe is the most common winter callout.
reels.instagram:
Every cold snap, half my callouts are the same thing — a frozen condensate pipe.

It's the white plastic pipe running outside. When it freezes the boiler locks out to protect itself.

Warm water (not boiling) poured along the pipe usually clears it, then reset the boiler. If it keeps happening, the pipe needs lagging or rerouting.

reels.hook: TRV numbers aren't a speed dial
reels.body: 3 doesn't heat the room faster than 5. It's a target, not a throttle.
reels.instagram:
The numbers on your radiator valve aren't speed settings.

They're target temperatures. Turning it to 5 doesn't heat the room faster — it just heats it to a higher temperature and keeps going longer.

Set it where the room's comfortable and leave it. That's what it's designed to do.

reels.hook: Same fault. Same boiler. Third time.
reels.body: If it keeps failing the same way, stop replacing the same part.

If a boiler keeps failing the same way, the part isn't the problem — something is killing that part.

Repeat PCB failures usually mean water getting somewhere it shouldn't. Repeat pump failures usually mean sludge.

Replacing the same component a third time isn't a repair, it's a subscription.
